domain: Biological Anthropology / Material Culture / Evolutionary Biology
topic_summary: Analysis of the overbite as a structural consequence of fork-and-knife adoption in Western Europe (~250 years ago) and chopstick adoption in China (~900 years earlier). C. Loring Brace's thesis: cutlery use eliminated the functional demand on anterior teeth, allowing overbite configuration to persist into adulthood through 'capacity by disuse.' Flagged as candidate for beneficiary-less path-naturalization.

key_entities: C. Loring Brace (American anthropologist, overbite-cutlery thesis originator)
Chopstick eating practice (China, ~900 years earlier adoption)
Edge-to-edge bite (ancestral human jaw configuration, ape-like)
Overbite (modern human jaw configuration, upper incisors overlap lower)
key_tensions: Functional demand vs structural persistence (anterior tooth use vs overbite configuration)
Cultural practice vs biological morphology (cutlery adoption vs jaw development)

axes.primary_observable: Frequency of anterior tooth loading during eating; archaeological jaw wear patterns pre/post-cutlery
axes.selection_reason: Upstream mountain; physical mechanism of functional displacement; feeds both downstream axes

axes.primary_observable: Age of cutlery adoption vs jaw configuration fixation timeline; comparative developmental studies

axes.structural_delta: Overbite configuration becomes population-normal through disuse of corrective mechanism, no actor benefits

axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; synthesis node testing beneficiary-less naturalization; piton hypothesis (atrophied capacity)

axes.selection_reason: Deferred: cultural mechanism upstream of functional displacement but lower structural distinctiveness

The 'bite-configuration commitment' is not a kernel with competing interpretations—it is a single biological outcome (overbite) with one causal pathway (functional disuse). No authority structure adjudicates 'legitimate' bite configurations. Collapse to ordinary axis decomposition.

Is beneficiary-less naturalization a valid constraint type, or does absence of beneficiary indicate misclassification? If every constraint requires a beneficiary, overbite_persistence_pathway may be a mountain (biological inevitability) rather than piton (atrophied capacity). Requires ontological clarification.

At what age does jaw configuration become irreversible? If adults can restore edge-to-edge bite through sustained anterior loading, developmental_window_closure is a rope (coordination problem) not a mountain (biological constraint). Empirical uncertainty.

Does the 900-year-earlier Chinese chopstick adoption show identical overbite timeline? If not, cultural_diffusion_mechanism may have higher epsilon than currently classified. Cross-cultural validation gap.
